scope: Read-only source diagnosis and synthetic startup characterization; no implementation, gameplay, network, model, SQL, world, private journal or configuration effects.

actual_evidence.cleanup: Supported cleanup and exact offline readback (existing receipt; no new SQL observation).
actual_evidence.limitation: Only last 16 headers and safe transport/vitals flags were saved. No raw payloads, full actors, readiness predicate values, inner exception message or traceback. Last 16 contain no 0ADF; this does not prove absence in all 67 frames.

findings.claim: The pilot requires exactly one current received NPC named Bard#brising within distance 3, plus canonical prt_fild08, known alive true, standing true, no stand/rest pending and confirmed arrival/no pending movement.

PlayingClient currently acquires NPC names only from validated 58-byte 0ADF name replies, name@10[24], after the same actor has already been received as presentation6/12. Actor entries retain species but not their supplied names. NPC#id fallback can never meet the pilot exact-name predicate.

Pinned server unsolicited actor-entry packets already include a name. Normal visible-area idle/new presentation calls clif_set_unit_idle, which fills p.name with status_get_name; BL_NPC returns npc_data.name. Thus the server need not send a separate unsolicited 0ADF to expose Bard. The client ignores this existing received name channel.

The inspected clif.cpp separate-name path calls clif_name from clif_parse_GetCharNameRequest; its NPC branch emits 0ADF. Normal getareachar BL_NPC handling does not call it. BotClient and PlayingClient have no automatic GetCharNameRequest path. A guaranteed unsolicited separate NPC name reply is not established.

The final post-20180307 profile registers 0x0368, six bytes, actor id@2 for GetCharNameRequest. Do not treat historical 0x0094 as the only profile authority. Both are denied by the current pilot post-connect transport scope; merely adding an auto-query would violate that scope.

The source Bard#brising token is the real display-name spelling, not a client-side public-source lookup permission. Script declaration has no :: alias; npc_parsename copies it unchanged to name/exname. Do not replace it with Bard based on visual client conventions.

Initial authentication 02EB establishes standing in wrapper metadata and arrival in tracker, so a movement command is not inherently required for startup NPC motion readiness. Vitals/healthy transport alone establish neither those receipts nor current map, progression, actor or life readiness.

causal_conclusion.confirmed: A deterministic received-name projection/acquisition gap blocks fixed-name startup when actor entries arrive without a separate 0ADF. The wait only retries; it neither consumes entry names nor requests the separate name channel.
causal_conclusion.not_proven: Whether that name gap was the exact failed predicate of the one native attempt; initial progression/perception/map/life/pose/motion/actor count/range remain unknown.
causal_conclusion.falsifier: A saved current actor-bound valid 0ADF with Bard#brising before timeout would disprove missing separate-name receipt as that run's failing predicate. It would not disprove the ignored entry-name defect.

offline_verification.limitations: Actual PlayingClient projection and ScheduledAgent wait with AST-extracted unchanged pilot predicates/transport guard; synthetic Wire, no native receiver or live-run replay. Fake clock shortens wait to 0.2 seconds. Native byte contents are unknown.
